Cloudflare Soars 6% as PHP Flaw Hitting 70% of Websites Lifts Security Stocks ©maxkabakov from Getty Images, Yuri_Arcurs from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Cloudflare stock rose 6% and Datadog rose 7% today after PHP patched two critical flaws in software that runs an estimated 70% of websites.

Cloudflare gave every customer firewall rules against the known attacks, including free users, which shows why its place in front of millions of sites is valuable.

Analysts expect Cloudflare's revenue to more than double, from $2.17 billion in 2025 to $4.73 billion in 2028.

The stock was already richly valued after a big run this year, so watch whether CISA lists the flaw and whether free users move to paid plans.

Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) stock jumped 6% today after PHP rushed out emergency patches for two critical flaws in the software behind an estimated 70% of the world's websites. Other stocks tied to protecting websites and apps rose too, including Datadog (DDOG:NASDAQ), up 7%.

What exactly happened

The flaws let an attacker take over any web server running PHP 5.4 or later. One of them can also leak passwords, session tokens and API keys. Security researcher Kevin Beaumont called it "one of the biggest vulns in years."

Attackers didn't wait for the fix. Cloudflare logged the first attacks at 3:43 a.m. ET, hours before the official patch landed around 10 a.m. ET.

Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht's response:

"PHP sites behind Cloudflare already have an initial set of WAF rules deployed for the known exploit vectors in these vulnerabilities. The rules are available to all customers, including free."

TIKR tracks 34 analysts on Cloudflare. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Cloudflare, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Cloudflare's Analyst Ratings

The free tier earns its keep

That last line is the story. Cloudflare sits in front of millions of PHP sites, so one set of rules covered all of them at once, before most of their owners could patch.

That's why it pays to give protection away. Every free site Cloudflare shields in a crisis like this one gives its owner a reason to stay, and eventually to pay.

And the paid business is growing fast. Analysts expect revenue to more than double, from $2.17 billion in 2025 to $4.73 billion in 2028…

Cloudflare (NET): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023–2028 (TIKR)

Nothing in today's news should move those estimates yet. That would take site owners signing up for paid plans after the scare, and the next few quarters will show whether they do.

A big day at a steep price

Today's pop comes right after Cloudflare dropped 15% in a week. Before that, a run had the stock up 78% since January by early October. Before today's move it already traded at nearly 200x forward earnings, and today's jump pushes that higher.

title: Are You Sure You Understand Cloudflare Stock's Risk?

Are You Sure You Understand Cloudflare Stock's Risk?

Image from Pixabay

Cloudflare (NET) stock returned 39.6% over the past year to October 19, 2026, compared with 17.4% for the S&P 500, and its sales grew 36% in fiscal Q2 2026. Numbers like those can make a stock look as if it has earned some calm. Yet the shares fell 15.2% in the week to October 19, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 1.5%. So how far has Cloudflare stock fallen when the whole market turned, and how long did it take to climb back from the low?

How Far Has Cloudflare Stock Fallen In Market Shocks?

It fell much further than the broader market. Across the six market shocks since Cloudflare listed in 2019, the stock fell 30.9% on average, compared with 16.8% for the S&P 500 over the same dates.

The steepest drop arrived during the 2022 inflation shock and Fed tightening, when Cloudflare stock fell 69% while the index lost 24%. The stock also fell 37% during the 2023 regional banking crisis, a period when the S&P 500 fell 6.7%.

Recovery times have varied widely. From its lowest close in each shock, Cloudflare stock required a median of 1.2 months to return to its earlier peak close. The 2022 fall took 31.4 months to erase, and the shares did not regain their March 2022 peak until January 2025.

Falls like this test every retirement plan. If your advisor recently retired, it is a good moment for a free second opinion from our partner firm.

Is Cloudflare's Business Growing Into A Profit?

Revenue is growing faster, but the company still reports a loss. Cloudflare generated $2.51 billion in revenue over the four quarters to June 30, 2026, up 33.5% from a year earlier. That pace topped the 27.3% growth recorded the year before. Management cited rapid growth in the Workers developer platform as the first among several drivers for the latest quarter.

Excluding restructuring charges, the operating loss shrank to 8.1% of revenue over the latest four quarters, from 9.9% a year earlier and 21.2% in the four quarters to June 2022. Including the $151 million of charges, it widened to 14.1% of revenue. Gross margin moved the other way, falling to 73% from 76.1% a year earlier, meaning the company keeps less of each sales dollar.

Cloudflare held more cash than debt at June 30, 2026, reporting $4.16 billion of cash and short-term investments against $3.53 billion of convertible notes and lease obligations. In August, Cloudflare repaid $1.29 billion of notes that matured.

Cloudflare Faces Higher Costs, Slower Growth And More Debt

Cloudflare is paying more than it planned to restructure its business. On the August 6, 2026 call, management said severance and other restructuring charges hit $151 million for fiscal Q2 2026, coming in higher than first expected. Without those charges, management said the quarter's reported net loss of $170 million would have been about $18 million. The company now expects up to $165 million of such charges for all of 2026.

Key Takeaways

Cloudflare stock fell 15% in the past week (through Monday's close), while the Nasdaq 100 fell 3.7%.

The company put out no bad news, and the drop looks like a better entry point into a business that's still growing fast.

A sell-off in AI and richly valued software stocks hit Cloudflare, Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike, and at about 200x forward earnings Cloudflare is still expensive.

Third-quarter results come after the close on Nov. 5, and the consensus price target sits about 15% above Monday's close.

Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) stock is down 15% in the past week (through Monday's close). That leaves it nearly 20% below the record high it hit on Oct. 6. The Nasdaq 100 lost 3.7% over the same stretch.

Even so, Cloudflare is still up 51% in 2026.

A bad week for anything priced for AI

Three sessions did almost all the damage: Cloudflare fell 6.7% on Oct. 14, 2.5% on Oct. 15 and 6.3% on Oct. 16, as inflation worries and rising bond yields sent investors out of AI names and richly valued software.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW:NASDAQ) fell 14.1% and CrowdStrike (CRWD:NASDAQ) 13.3% over the same week. Cloudflare fell more than either Palo Alto or CrowdStrike, and it had the most to lose. At about 200x forward earnings, most of what buyers pay for sits years out, and higher yields make those years worth less today.

The company gave nobody a reason to sell

Cloudflare agreed to buy Deno to improve its Workers programming model. On Monday it also expanded the partner lineup for Cloudflare OS, its AI workspace.

Analysts kept raising their targets, too: BTIG, Oppenheimer, Barclays and TD Cowen lifted theirs between Oct. 6 and Oct. 13, to between $375 and $430.

As SaaStr founder Jason Lemkin put it on the 20VC podcast on Oct. 15: "They beat the quarter. They've accelerated growth even more." Second-quarter revenue rose 36% to $696.1 million.

Nov. 5 is the next test

Cloudflare reports third-quarter results after the close on Thursday, Nov. 5. Management guided for $736.0 million to $737.0 million of revenue, and Oppenheimer expects Cloudflare to beat that as more customers adopt its security products.

Analysts expect revenue to grow 32% this year, to $2.87 billion, and another 29% in 2027.

Cloudflare (NET): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024–2029 (TIKR)

That 2026 estimate is already at the top of management's full-year range, so Cloudflare needs a beat on Nov. 5.

Cheaper, but still not cheap

At about 200x forward earnings, Cloudflare is still expensive. But the Street's consensus target kept climbing into the drop.

Cloudflare (NET): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

At $343, the target sits about 15% above Monday's close.

title: What Does GoDaddy Offer That Akamai Does Not?

What Does GoDaddy Offer That Akamai Does Not?

Image from Pixabay

Akamai Technologies (AKAM) and GoDaddy (GDDY) are both bought to capture the same trend: businesses paying for AI over the internet. Akamai sells the computing power for AI through its cloud infrastructure services. GoDaddy sells its AI tools, called Airo, to the small businesses that already buy its domains. One company is building new capacity, while the other sells from a platform it already runs. What did each company tell the market in its latest report?

What Akamai And GoDaddy Have Told Investors Since July

At the midpoint of its guidance range, Akamai management trimmed its full-year 2026 revenue forecast on August 6 to $4.488 billion, down from $4.498 billion projected in May. Management also said it expects overall revenue growth to accelerate into the low teens in 2027. More than $2.8 billion of multiyear commitments signed in 2026 back that expectation. On September 24, the company added that a customer agreed to an $11.6 billion, seven-year commitment for cloud services. This commitment arrived seven weeks after the 2027 forecast.

GoDaddy offered a different update on July 30. Management narrowed the company's full-year 2026 revenue guidance to between $5.215 billion and $5.255 billion. This left the midpoint unchanged from April, and executives reaffirmed its free cash flow target of about $1.8 billion. Akamai pairs a slightly lower 2026 forecast with expectations for faster growth in 2027. GoDaddy presents a 2026 plan that remains intact.

Choices like this test every retirement plan. If your advisor recently retired, it is a good moment for a free second opinion from our partner firm.

Akamai Spends On AI While GoDaddy Buys Back Shares

Akamai is paying for that growth up front. Management expects capital spending to reach about 40% of revenue in 2026. At the midpoint of the company's guidance, this equals roughly $1.8 billion, about as much as GoDaddy expects to generate in free cash flow. Akamai raised $3.5 billion of zero-coupon convertible debt in May to help fund the build-out, even as it continued share repurchases, spending $410 million in the second quarter. Total debt at Akamai now stands at 74.0% of its market value, compared with 27.5% for GoDaddy.

Akamai reported an 11.9% operating margin over the four quarters to June 2026, down from 15.4% a year earlier. Management said the second-quarter results include expanded colocation investments and higher depreciation, taken on to fuel growth in its cloud infrastructure services.

GoDaddy's operating margin moved the other direction, climbing to 25.2% over the same four quarters from 21.8% a year earlier. Rather than pausing buybacks, GoDaddy spent $554 million on its own shares in the second quarter.

title: Is Cloudflare (NET) Worth It When Most of Its Users Pay Nothing?

Cloudflare, Inc. (NYSE:NET) closed at $297.58 on October 19. The stock returned 45.3% over the last 6 months, compared with an 11.6% return for the Insider Monkey Billionaire Index and 8.7% for the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust.

Cloudflare sits between a website and the people visiting it, speeding up what it can and blocking what it should. Millions of sites use it, and most of them pay nothing. That free tier is the reason the company has the reach it does, and it is also why the price is harder to justify than the business is to admire.

READ ALSO: 10 Best Stocks to Buy for High Returns in 2026

Is Cloudflare (NET) Worth It When Most of Its Users Pay Nothing?
What the Free Tier Buys:

Giving the basic service away put Cloudflare in front of an enormous number of sites at almost no selling cost. The paying customers come largely from inside that pool. It works as a growth engine.

Turnover jumped 35.90% over the most recent quarter, carrying the company towards $2.87 billion in revenue this year, which is unusual for a business selling infrastructure rather than applications.

Cloudflare is one of the ten in our 10 Most Promising Cloud Stocks According to Hedge Funds. To see the rest of the list, click HERE.

What It Costs:

Serving customers who pay nothing is not free. The network has to be built and run for all of them, which is why the company still reports an operating margin of -7.60% at this scale. Debt sits at 217.86% of equity, heavy for a business that has not yet made a profit. The cash flow is positive, so this is a question of patience rather than survival.

The model also caps the price of the paid product. A customer who can see a capable free version has a reference point every time the bill arrives.

DON'T MISS: 10 AI Stocks Beyond NVIDIA That Could Surge in 2026

Good or Bad at This Price:

At 178.57 times what analysts expect next year the price is the hard part. The stock is up 45.3% over six months. The business is good, and the price is the problem.

At this level, a buyer is not paying for what Cloudflare earns but for what it might earn if the free users keep converting for another decade. Paying this much for a business still losing money is one way to back it. 11 Best SaaS Stocks to Buy Right Now sets out the cheaper ones.

Conclusion:

The business deserves the admiration, but the stock is a hard buy at this level. Giving the core product away is what gave Cloudflare its reach, and the growth rate shows the strategy working exactly as intended. The difficulty is that the same free users have to be served whether they pay or not, which is why the margin is still negative at this size. The price then assumes a decade of conversion going right. Watch the paid customer count rather than the revenue, since that is the number the whole model turns on.

Cloudflare (NET) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Over the past month, shares of this web security and content delivery company have returned -15.4%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +0.7% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which Cloudflare falls in, has gained 2.2%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Cloudflare is expected to post earnings of $0.35 per share, indicating a change of +29.6% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $1.26 points to a change of +35.5% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has remained unchanged.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $1.72 indicates a change of +36.2% from what Cloudflare is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has remained unchanged.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Cloudflare.
